what: GLM-5.3-Flash decode kernels. Every dimension is a metadata key from the model's own GGUF, read on 2026-11-02 -- none is chosen and none is inferred from a tensor shape.
shapes_source: the GLM-5.3-Flash-Q2 GGUF's own metadata keys (`glm5-next.*`), read with the engine's metadata dumper on 2026-11-02. Every value below is a key from that file, not a tensor-shape inference and not a choice.
architecture_note: `glm5-next` is a hybrid and the corpus reflects it: 34 of 46 blocks use a gated delta net, 12 use MLA, 43 FFNs are a 288-expert MoE and 3 are dense, and there is NO RoPE (rope_dimension_count = 0). This is a different architecture from GLM-5.2's `glm-dsa`, which is why the engine path that reads `glm-dsa.*` keys cannot load this model.

not_in_this_corpus.kda_recurrence: the delta-net state update -- a sequential scan with a decay term. The tile API has no recurrent-scan intrinsic: every op in it is a whole-tile map or reduction, and a scan is neither.
not_in_this_corpus.kda_short_conv: the depthwise causal convolution over 4 timesteps. The tile API has no sliding-window intrinsic, and expressing it as a matmul would change the arithmetic and the memory traffic both.
not_in_this_corpus.why_omitted: Approximating either would put a kernel in this corpus that computes something the model does not. Two thirds of this model's blocks use them, so the corpus covers the parts that are expressible and says plainly that it does not cover the rest.

representations.tile: generated by bench/shapes/gen_glm_5_3.py from the registry's sourced shapes.
representations.pto: from the in-tree rspto. Reproducible; a test asserts it byte for byte.
representations.tile-rs: Rust source against the tile intrinsics, lifted from the .pto by the in-tree ptoas-rs. COMPILED: a test checks every file in this column against the kernel-side DSL, and a second test checks that the lift still accepts the .pto it came from. Two of the eight kernels are here; the other six are refused by the lift for reasons its own census names.
representations.searched: for a refused kernel, the tiling tile-search chose instead.

tile_rs_removed_2026_11_02.why: They did not compile, and the lift can no longer produce them. Each stored a 1x1 reduce result through `tile_store_f32::<8, 1>` -- `expected 8, found 1` -- because the emitter read a tile_buf's `rows`/`cols`, the extent ALLOCATED against the 512-byte fractal, where `v_row`/`v_col` carries the logical shape. The lift now refuses those `.pto` artifacts by name ('tile `%pto8` has a partial or dynamic v_row'), so these files are output of a generator that no longer exists in that form. Found by compiling the corpus for the first time, which only became possible when the kernel-side DSL was carried into this tree.
tile_rs_removed_2026_11_02.to_restore: Thread the valid extent through the emitter instead of the allocated one, then prove on hardware that the store writes one element and not eight. Until that is measured, a refusal is worth more than a kernel that compiles and writes the wrong count.

estimated_decode_kernels.source: derived from the model's own configuration by inventory(); a LOWER BOUND, because the inventory predicted 15 for DeepSeek V4 Flash against a registry count of 52, so it under-counts by about 3.5x. Not applied as a correction: one anchor cannot calibrate a model, and a derivation multiplied by 3.5 would look measured and would not be.
estimated_decode_kernels.what_it_is: The number of distinct kernels one decode step of this model needs -- the denominator the representation counts are read against. Where the count is KNOWN it is used; where it is not, inventory() derives a LOWER BOUND from the model's own configuration. Not a measurement of a running engine in either case.
estimated_decode_kernels.derivation_error: the inventory predicted 15 for DeepSeek V4 Flash against a registry count of 52, so it under-counts by about 3.5x. Not applied as a correction: one anchor cannot calibrate a model, and a derivation multiplied by 3.5 would look measured and would not be.
estimated_decode_kernels.a_kernel_is: one distinct (operation, shape) pair, because that is what this corpus holds -- one rmsnorm file serves every block that shares D. A layer count does not multiply it.

inventory.line: rmsnorm at D (attn_norm, ffn_norm and the final norm share it)
MLA projections: q_a, q_b, kv_a, kv_b, output
second attention core: the gated delta net
routed expert gate/up at MOE_INTER, and down at D
the leading dense blocks' gate/up at DENSE_FFN_INTER, and down at D

estimated_decode_kernels.reconciliation: 15 kernels present + the rows named above = the DERIVED inventory total of 20. It does not reconcile against 20 when that is a lower bound from another source, and it is not meant to: the gaps were enumerated against the inventory.

what_the_inventory_collapses.each expert's gate, up and down are one: a real engine has three kernels there, and the gate/up pair is often fused separately from the down-projection
what_the_inventory_collapses.one attention core: decode, prefill and partial/chunked are different kernels with different shapes, and a model with two attention types doubles that again
what_the_inventory_collapses.one matvec per projection: f16 and f32 weight forms are separate kernels, and each quantisation the engine supports adds another (q8_0, q4_K, iq2_xxs, mxfp4 ...)
what_the_inventory_collapses.no prefill shapes: every projection and norm has a batched prefill form, which is a different kernel from its decode form
what_the_inventory_collapses.no quantise/dequantise kernels: activation quantisation and weight unpacking are real kernels; the inventory treats weight format as out of scope
what_the_inventory_collapses.one sampling kernel: argmax is counted; top-p, top-k sampling and draft verification are not

estimated_decode_kernels.why_collapses_are_listed_not_multiplied: 'under-counts by 3.5x' is one number and tells a reader nothing they can act on. These name the specific rows that each stand for several real kernels. They are not multiplied out: that would turn a list of known omissions into a fabricated total. Someone who knows the true count for this model can see which rows to expand.
estimated_decode_kernels.published_registry: the published kernel registry, read 2026-11-02, holds 6 distinct kernels for this model, all of them model-prefixed and all under a `source-scan` basis. That is FEWER than this manifest's derived lower bound, and the registry was generated 2026-08-31, before this architecture's work landed. The derived bound therefore stands: adopting a smaller external figure would lower a bound on the strength of its provenance alone. The 6 is recorded as a floor on model-specific kernels alone.
